SWISS-MONO FONT SUBSET MANIFEST
===============================

Source of the requested set: plan-pi-dashboard-swiss-mono-layout.md, "Subset
spec". This file is the source of truth the test pins against
(tests/test_swiss_fonts.py); the vendored woff2 cmaps must match it exactly.

Kept SEPARATE from subset-manifest.txt (the HUD's): the two layouts need
different unicode sets, and tests/test_hud_fonts.py parses a SINGLE --unicodes=
line out of that file - a second line would break it. One vendored-font home
(static/vendor/fonts/), two manifests, two independent pins.

Fonts (both SIL OFL 1.1, self-hosted, no CDN):
  Inter          400/600/800 + 700  -> inter-{400,600,700,800}.woff2
  JetBrains Mono 500 + 700           -> jetbrains-mono-{500,700}.woff2

Weights are exactly those design-mocks/swiss-mono.html uses:
  Inter (--grot): 400 (red hero degree .deg), 600 (condition / meta value /
    event title), 700 (clock / forecast high / agenda day), 800 (hero temp).
  JetBrains Mono (--mono): 500 (most mono runs), 700 (forecast day / pill /
    NOW tag / REFRESH / precip emphasis).

Upstream / provenance:
  Inter - google/fonts ofl/inter/Inter[opsz,wght].ttf (variable)
  JetBrains Mono - JetBrains/JetBrainsMono fonts/ttf/{Medium,Bold}.ttf
The license texts are vendored alongside (OFL-Inter.txt, OFL-JetBrains-Mono.txt).
The .woff2 here are pyftsubset cuts of those upstreams, NOT the full fonts.
@font-face wiring lives in fonts.css; the swiss-mono layout is the only consumer.

Regeneration:
  Inter is a variable font, so each weight is first INSTANCED to a static
  master before subsetting:
    fontTools.varLib.instancer  ->  wght=<W>, opsz=14   (the text optical master)
  then every face is subset identically:

  --unicodes=U+0020-007E,U+00B0,U+00B7,U+2191,U+2193,U+25CF
  --flavor=woff2 --layout-features='tnum' --no-hinting --desubroutinize

NOTE on --layout-features: 'tnum' (tabular figures - the mock sets
font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums), NOT the HUD's '*'. Inter carries a huge
OpenType feature set (20 stylistic sets, fractions, char variants); retaining
'*' drags their entire alternate-glyph closure into the cut (~10x larger files)
for glyphs this design never renders. The subsetter still keeps the always-on
default features. Only the cmap is pinned by the test, so this is safe.

REQUESTED characters
  - Basic Latin  U+0020-U+007E  (printable ASCII: includes mono digits 0-9 and %)
  - U+00B0  °  DEGREE SIGN
  - U+00B7  ·  MIDDLE DOT
  - U+2191  ↑  UPWARDS ARROW      ("+N earlier" summary line)
  - U+2193  ↓  DOWNWARDS ARROW    ("+N more" / "+N more days" lines)
  - U+25CF  ●  BLACK CIRCLE       ("● NOW" tag)

SELF_HOSTED_MARKS (non-ASCII marks the design renders, present in EVERY subset):
  ° · ↑ ↓ ●
Unlike the HUD (whose ◆ ▸ ◂ ▲ ▼ ⟳ are absent from its mono fonts and had to be
drawn as SVG), fontTools confirmed all three marks ↑ ↓ ● exist in both Inter and
JetBrains Mono, so swiss-mono needs NO SVG fallback - they subset directly.

FALLBACK_SYMBOLS: none. Every mark the design emits is vendored above.
